bio: A meal in this attractive eatery, amusingly adorned with a collection of hens, followed by a restful night in one of the guestrooms of the bustling country inn, are just the ticket to get better acquainted with the picturesque Semois valley. The chef is an unabashed fan of tradition and his region, as the menu demonstrates. How about Clamart pigeon in a gutsy gravy made from the bones? Or what about a fresh salad of lobster tail paired with velvety foie gras, grey shrimp and a herby dressing? Blatantly and indulgently generous to the delight of lovers of down to earth, rustic fare. You can’t go wrong with the set menu, which offers a number of choices, although you could also treat yourself to one of the house lobster signature dishes…...
